properties.name: A refused relation word gets the review vocabulary with its glosses cut short, and no pointer to the tool that draws what the word meant
properties.statement:
Field log entry 2026-10-09 (hxm_program hub, VS Code 1.140, reflow2 0.80.0): add_decision related_to relation "governs" was refused, the allowed values were "cut off mid-list in the terminal", and none fitted "this decision governs a Component", so the reporter wrote a no_relation_note instead.

MEASURED 2026-10-09 on 0.80.0 and main (same output): exit 2; the reply lists all 13 allowed values, CONTRADICTS through VIOLATES, then their one-line glosses, and reflow2 itself cuts the glosses mid-list ("…they were…"). So the list was whole, and the cut the reporter saw is reflow2's, in the glosses.

NEITHER VERSION NAMES governed_by, the tool that draws what the word meant (a Component GOVERNED_BY a Decision). The schema refusal answers "which values does this field take". It never answers "where does what you meant go" when the word names an edge type another tool draws: governs, satisfies, realizes, allocates, decomposes. The reporter's intended link was not recorded; a note stands in its place.
